description: The Hybrid Intelligence authors publish Julia and SciML code for controlling a three-node water network with a physics-based differential-algebraic model and neural components. The 2026 Zenodo release includes synthetic SCADA, trained pump and leakage components in BSON, and Julia functions for calibration and control experiments. The public README requires Julia 1.7 or later. Zenodo states CC BY 4.0 and provides a free archive; the GitHub API exposes no separate repository licence. These materials can compare hydraulic constraints, learned components and operating costs in water-network simulations. Real SCADA is withheld under a nondisclosure agreement, and regenerating the synthetic data from its original source therefore requires unavailable inputs. Pregenerated synthetic data are included, while noise estimation contains a placeholder. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this implementation. Reported cost reductions and safety performance remain unverified; no model was executed.
